describe.open: Open a file, returning a file descriptor. `flags` defaults to `'r'` and `mode` defaults to `0o666`. `flags` may be a string such as `'r'`, `'w'`, `'a'`, `'r+'`, etc., or a numeric combination of `fs.constants` flags.
describe.access: Check whether the file at `filepath` is accessible. `mode` defaults to `fs.constants.F_OK`.
describe.exists: Check whether a file exists at `filepath`. Returns `true` if the file is accessible, `false` otherwise.
describe.read: Read from a file descriptor into `buffer`. `offset` defaults to `0`, `len` defaults to `buffer.byteLength - offset`, and `pos` defaults to `-1` (current position). Returns the number of bytes read.
describe.readv: Read from a file descriptor into an array of `buffers`. `pos` defaults to `-1`.
describe.write: Write `data` to a file descriptor. When `data` is a string, the signature is `fs.write(fd, data[, pos[, encoding]])` where `encoding` defaults to `'utf8'`. Returns the number of bytes written.
describe.writev: Write an array of `buffers` to a file descriptor. `pos` defaults to `-1`.
describe.stat: Get the status of a file. Returns a `Stats` object.
describe.lstat: Like `fs.stat()`, but if `filepath` is a symbolic link, the link itself is statted, not the file it refers to.
describe.fstat: Get the status of a file by its file descriptor. Returns a `Stats` object.
describe.statfs: Get filesystem statistics. Returns a `StatFs` object.
describe.ftruncate: Truncate a file to `len` bytes. `len` defaults to `0`.
describe.chmod: Change the permissions of a file. `mode` may be a numeric mode or a string that will be parsed as octal.
describe.fchmod: Change the permissions of a file by its file descriptor.
describe.chown: Change the owner and group of a file.
describe.lchown: Change the owner and group of a file, but if `filepath` is a symbolic link, the changes are applied only to the link, not the file it refers to.
describe.fchown: Change the owner and group of a file by its file descriptor.
describe.utimes: Change the access and modification times of a file. Times may be numbers (seconds since epoch) or `Date` objects.
describe.lutimes: Like `fs.utimes()`, but if `filepath` is a symbolic link, the timestamps of the link is changed, not the file it refers to.
describe.futimes: Change the access and modification times of a file by its file descriptor. Times may be numbers (seconds since epoch) or `Date` objects.
describe.link: Creates a new link (also known as a hard link) to an existing file.
describe.rm: Remove a file or directory at `filepath`.
describe.copyFile: Copy a file from `src` to `dst`. `mode` is an optional bitmask created from `fs.constants.COPYFILE_EXCL`, `fs.constants.COPYFILE_FICLONE`, or `fs.constants.COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE`.
describe.cp: Copy a file or directory from `src` to `dst`.
describe.realpath: Resolve the real path of `filepath`, expanding all symbolic links.
describe.readlink: Read the target of a symbolic link.
describe.truncate: Truncate the file at `filename` to `len` bytes. `len` defaults to `0`.
describe.symlink: Create a symbolic link at `filepath` pointing to `target`. `type` may be `'file'`, `'dir'`, or `'junction'` (Windows only) or a numeric flag. On Windows, if `type` is not provided, it is inferred from the target.
describe.fsync: Flush all modified in-core data of the file referred by its file descriptor to the disk device.
describe.fdatasync: Similar to `fsync`, but does not flush modified metadata unless necessary.
describe.opendir: Open a directory for iteration. Returns a `Dir` object.
describe.readdir: Read the contents of a directory. Returns an array of filenames or, if `withFileTypes` is `true`, an array of `Dirent` objects.
describe.readFile: Read the entire contents of a file. Returns a `Buffer` by default, or a string if an `encoding` is specified.
describe.writeFile: Write `data` to a file, replacing it if it already exists.
describe.appendFile: Append `data` to a file, creating it if it does not exist. Accepts the same options as `fs.writeFile()` but defaults to the `'a'` flag.
describe.watch: Watch a file or directory for changes. Returns a `Watcher` object. The `callback`, if provided, is called with `(eventType, filename)` on each change.
describe.createReadStream: Create a readable stream for a file. Returns a `ReadStream`.
describe.createWriteStream: Create a writable stream for a file. Returns a `WriteStream`.
describe.constants: An object containing file system constants. See `fs/constants` for the full list. Commonly used constants include:
describe.uid: The user identifier of the file owner.
describe.gid: The group identifier of the file owner.
describe.rdev: The device identifier for special files.
describe.blksize: The file system block size for I/O operations.
describe.size: The size of the file in bytes.
describe.atimeMs: The access time in milliseconds since the epoch.
describe.mtimeMs: The modification time in milliseconds since the epoch.
describe.ctimeMs: The change time in milliseconds since the epoch.
describe.birthtimeMs: The creation time in milliseconds since the epoch.
describe.atime: The access time as a `Date` object.
describe.mtime: The modification time as a `Date` object.
describe.ctime: The change time as a `Date` object.
describe.birthtime: The creation time as a `Date` object.
describe.isDirectory: Returns `true` if the file is a directory.
describe.isFile: Returns `true` if the file is a regular file.
describe.isBlockDevice: Returns `true` if the file is a block device.
describe.isCharacterDevice: Returns `true` if the file is a character device.
describe.isFIFO: Returns `true` if the file is a FIFO (named pipe).
describe.isSymbolicLink: Returns `true` if the file is a symbolic link. Only meaningful when using `fs.lstat()`.
describe.isSocket: Returns `true` if the file is a socket.
describe.parentPath: The path of the parent directory.
describe.name: The name of the directory entry, as a string or `Buffer` depending on the encoding.
describe.type: The numeric type of the directory entry.
describe.flags: The flags the file was opened with.
describe.ref: Prevent the event loop from exiting while the watcher is active.
describe.unref: Allow the event loop to exit even if the watcher is still active.
